_comment: The M1 fixed prompt set. Each case targets a distinct failure mode; do not prune this list to make a phase pass.

cases.prompt: Operating systems solved the equivalent problem decades ago. Physical memory is cut into fixed-size pages, each process holds a page table mapping its virtual addresses onto whichever physical pages happen to be free, and fragmentation collapses from an external problem to an internal one bounded by the size of a single page. The same construction applies directly to the key-value cache of a transformer, and the reason it applies is that
cases.why: long prefill; catches position-id bugs that short prompts hide

cases.prompt: Once upon a time, in a distant kingdom,
cases.why: must terminate on EOS well before max_tokens. GPT-2 greedy essentially never emits <|endoftext|>, so the stop token is overridden to 11 (a comma), which this prompt reaches at position 6. Without the override nothing tests the termination path that every later phase reimplements by hand.

cases.prompt: Once upon a time, in a distant kingdom,
cases.why: must stop exactly at the limit; off-by-one on the final token shows up here

cases.why: degenerate case; the decode loop must handle zero iterations after prefill
